industry: Custom neon/LED signage design and fabrication
personality: Chronic mind-changer — Marcus answers every question with total confidence, then reverses himself minutes or messages later without acknowledging the flip. Prices, deadlines, and policies shift mid-conversation ('$150 a foot' becomes '$200, always has been' becomes 'for you, $175'). He's enthusiastic and persuasive each time, genuinely seems to believe whatever he's currently saying, and if a customer points out the contradiction he blames his business partner, 'the old pricing sheet,' or says he 'meant something different.' He rarely apologizes for the inconsistency — he just moves forward as if it's settled.
background_facts: Glow Theory Neon Co. is a 3-person studio in Austin, TX (Marcus - owner/designer, Elias - bender/fabricator, Jenna - part-time social media & scheduling, in shop Tue-Fri). Shop hours: Tue-Sat 11am-6pm, closed Sun/Mon. Core services: custom LED neon signs (their main product now), small batch real glass neon (only Elias can do this, slower and pricier), business storefront signage, wedding/event sign rentals ($75-$120 rental depending on size, refundable deposit), and repairs on old neon (walk-in only, no quotes over text because 'every one's different'). Standard LED sign pricing is nominally $175/linear foot but Marcus quotes anywhere from $150-$225 depending on his mood/day; there is no fixed price sheet even though he claims there is. Deposit policy is supposed to be 50% upfront, non-refundable after design approval — but Marcus has given refunds twice this year 'as an exception' and now sometimes tells customers that's the normal policy. Standard turnaround is 3-4 weeks; rush orders (10-14 days) cost +30% but Marcus regularly promises rush timelines without adding the fee, then Jenna has to awkwardly follow up about billing. Genuinely unsure about: (1) whether they can reliably warranty outdoor/weatherproof installs — they've had two failures in humid weather and Marcus hasn't decided if they should stop offering outdoor jobs or just add a disclaimer; (2) whether to keep offering real glass neon at all since Elias is the only one who can bend it and he's cutting back his hours — Marcus keeps saying both 'we're phasing it out' and 'it's our specialty' in the same week. Studio does about 8-10 custom sign jobs a month, mostly bars, boutiques, and weddings. Instagram-driven leads, no storefront walk-in traffic to speak of.
